symptom: An integration resolves the veBTC address from the official Mezo Pools governance table and reaches a different voter generation than the deployed PoolsVoter uses.
prerequisites: The integration selected the published veBTC address without resolving the current PoolsVoter graph.
The operation depends on current pools voting or boost topology.
diagnosticSteps: Assert Mezo mainnet identity and select one fixed block.
Resolve the current PoolsVoter proxy implementation, then read PoolsVoter.ve() at that block.
Resolve the returned ve proxy implementation and its voter/booster references before comparing the documentation table.
expected: The documentation table and deployed PoolsVoter graph identify the same current veBTC generation.
observed: At the recorded block, PoolsVoter.ve() returned 0x3d4b...f279 while the official Mezo Pools page printed 0x7d80...5914.
control: The returned ve contract identifies itself as veBTC, points back to the same PoolsVoter, and points to the deployed BoostVoter; the official explorer resolves its EIP-1967 implementation.
verifiedCause: The published governance address table lags the deployed PoolsVoter graph. This establishes stale identity documentation, not the product intent or lifecycle of the older generation.
safeMitigation: Resolve stable registry IDs once contract registry review promotes the graph. Until then, fail closed and use block-pinned deployed references only for investigation; do not ship writes from either raw address. For behavioral analysis, require either fully verified version-matched source or the recorded independent executable-bytecode reproduction; never silently upgrade the explorer's partial-verification label.
limitations: This is a point-in-time mainnet identity conflict and must be rechecked after upgrades.

The explorer still labels current veBTC and veMEZO source partially verified. Independent builds reproduce the deployed executables exactly, which establishes scoped behavior but not authorship, audit coverage, or proxy activation history.
